title: The console works on IP:8000, but on my domain the page loads without styles or logo
symptom: http://<server-ip>:8000 looks fine. https://<your-domain> shows plain text, no colours, no logo. A reverse proxy on the server (aaPanel, nginx, Apache) forwards the domain to port 8000.
solution:
**Cause:** the proxy does not pass the real host name and HTTPS to the console, so the page links its styles to `http://localhost` or `http://127.0.0.1:8000`, which the browser cannot load.

Check which address the page uses.

Linux:

```bash
curl -s https://<your-domain>/ | grep -o 'href="[^"]*atglance.css[^"]*"'
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
(Invoke-WebRequest https://<your-domain>/ -UseBasicParsing).Content | Select-String 'href="[^"]*atglance.css[^"]*"' | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches.Value }
```

It should start with `https://<your-domain>/`. If it shows `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `http://`, follow these steps.

### 1. Pass the host name and HTTPS through the proxy

**nginx:** use this location block in the site config, then run `nginx -t && nginx -s reload`.

```nginx
location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8000;
    proxy_set_header Host              $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host  $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port  $server_port;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP         $remote_addr;
}
```

**aaPanel:** open the site, Reverse proxy, then edit the proxy for `/`:

- Reverse proxy tab: keep the target `http://127.0.0.1:8000` and set Send Host to `$host`. Save.
- Config tab: paste the three lines below and save. Leave out X-Forwarded-For; aaPanel already sets it.

```nginx
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Port $server_port;
```

**Apache:** in the HTTPS virtual host, next to `ProxyPass / http://127.0.0.1:8000/`, add:

```apache
ProxyPreserveHost On
RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https"
```

### 2. Let the console trust the proxy

The proxy reaches the console from the Docker network, which it does not trust by default. Run on the server.

Linux:

```bash
docker exec ce-atglance-app sh -c 'echo "ATGLANCE_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1,::1,172.16.0.0/12" >> /app/storage/.env'
cd /opt/atglance && docker compose restart app worker scheduler
```

Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
docker exec ce-atglance-app sh -c 'echo "ATGLANCE_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1,::1,172.16.0.0/12" >> /app/storage/.env'
cd C:\ProgramData\AtGlance; docker compose restart app worker scheduler
```

### 3. Set the domain in the console

Log in on `http://<server-ip>:8000` as the super admin:

- Site Settings → Plugins: turn on **Custom Domain & HTTPS**.
- Site → Access URL: enter your domain, without `http://` and without a port.
- HTTPS: choose **Handled by my platform**, because your proxy holds the certificate. Save.

### 4. Check again

Run the check command again. It should now show `https://<your-domain>/css/atglance.css`. Reload the page with Ctrl+F5.

Servers running the atglance CLI still connect on port 8002 of the same host. Keep that port open; the domain only fronts the web console.
